title: How do you handle “vibe coded” feedback on an AI-assisted game? Looking for honest feedback.
author: Bromighty12
selftext:
I recently launched my dungeon-defense game, DelveKin, and got a few comments immediately calling it “vibe coded” or “AI looking.” One person even said they recognized the UI as Claude-generated despite me never using Claude.

To be transparent, I **did use AI tools to assist with coding as it greatly sped up development, since I’m doing this solo**, but there was a lot of hands on work designing, testing, balancing, and iterating on the game. Others may feel similarly, but despite the ai code assistance, there was a lot of work put in to ship the game. 

The visuals aren’t generated images either they’re Flutter CustomPainter/vector shapes.

I’m not looking to argue with the criticism. I’m curious what people here think:

• What about the game looks “vibe coded,” if anything?  
• Is it the art, UI, animations, or maybe the trailer itself?  
• How do other AI-assisted devs handle this kind of feedback?  
• Anything you’d change to make the game feel more distinctive?

Also curious what you think of the actual game/trailer outside of the AI discussion.  
I’m working on another mobile game now, so I’d rather learn from the feedback than ignore it.

Here are the links:

App Store:  
[https://apps.apple.com/us/app/delvekin-dungeon-defense/id6797352090](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/delvekin-dungeon-defense/id6797352090)  
Google Play:  
[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cindercode.delvekin](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cindercode.delvekin)

Thank you!

comments.author: TheReviewerWildTake
comments.body:
AI loves this type of pallet and UI, but tbh, it loves it because a lot of ppl used it and created tons of UIs in that style - which in turn was then fed to AI...   
  
So, it is one of those things that are just "common enough for AI to generate".

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body:
Problem with every "vibe coded" game is that UI gives it away the first second you look at it, because proper UI requires custom artwork in the same style across entire game which can be tricky with AI but still doable, definitely not just "coded" UI that you gave to AI to entirely do on it's own in the code. For proper UI you will need some training and a lot of tweaks but even starting with custom art will improve it a lot. If you use Codex you can ask it to generate art itself, if you use codex maybe best way is to pay 5$ on OpenAI API and give Codex access via API key.

Start with simple things like generating backgrounds and borders. I recently changed entire UI of "Ship" page in my game and now it went from this to this:

https://reddit.com/link/pd1c4hs/video/g87acmsbtosh1/player

  
I feel this helps massively in games not looking Vibe Coded. Obviously that is just one of many things, but it helps.

replies.author: Bromighty12
replies.body: This is very helpful! Yes, that seems to be my issue. Flutter custom painters is common in apps for UI and dialog styles, so I need to improve that presentation.

comments.author: Dramatic_Leopard679
comments.body: in addition to RUSuper 's suggestions, I say change the font and reduce the amount of text if possible; in actual ai's, most of the time it's just symbols and it gives you the explanation when you hover/click on them. ai though doesn't have this instinct and doesn't shy away from text. also, try to not use the dark mode blue/orange color palette and hard rectangles.

comments.author: mithrilsoft
comments.body:
I try to eliminate as much as possible anything that looks or feels AI. That 100% looks likes something Gemini canvas would make. Including colors, layout, and shapes. I use a lot of Unity Assets and have a policy of trying to alter anything that I use in a game, even if it's just changing colors or applying a shader. For AI projects, I create a look and feel design document that I make the AI follow. 

Otherwise I would just the state the facts and be truthful.

comments.author: JorgitoEstrella
comments.body: The gameplay looks fun for a mobile game but yes it looks completely vibe coded, like something you do in 1 prompt and don't polish it further.

replies.author: Bromighty12
replies.body: Appreciate the feedback! I feel like the trailer is failing to do it justice as well. There was a lot of polish on the strategy and gameplay elements. Like months of work. It’s sad to hear it gives off a one prompt vibe.

replies.author: JorgitoEstrella
replies.body:
Gemini gave me the same AI when I was one-prompt testing small games like snake, space invader, etc.

Just change the UI because it looks like very low effort vibes.

replies.author: Bromighty12
replies.body: Thank you. Thats helpful. May I ask what looks low effort? What parts do you recommend me focusing on? Appreciate your feedback!

replies.author: JorgitoEstrella
replies.body: The UI as I said looks like something you get from one-prompt shooting anything.

replies.author: Otterly_Delicious
replies.body: I think it is the minimalism of it, no texture, basic shapes.

replies.author: Easy_Cash_5395
replies.body: If it looks like the game in the trailer, it's going to be referred to the same way.

comments.author: Bromighty12
comments.body:
Does this help improve the presentation? I applied my background atmosphere which changes based on the dungeon level and added more shapes, textures and consistency around room colors. Thanks for the feedback!
